lessons.rule:
Main-hand levels are the second engine (+6 levels is about +1.3 blinds).
- Choose the main hand by how often you can draw it with 2 discards: you should be able to draw it in 3 of 4 hands. How often you have played it so far does not matter, unless you own Telescope (its pack planet is for your most played hand).
- Pair is the default once the board has +Mult or chips jokers. It is always drawable, and Sly, Jolly, Duo, Half Joker and Mercury support it. On a blank board (no jokers), Pair is not the plan; see the in-blind pace rule. Leave Pair only for a real signal: Spare Trousers, or a hand-type joker plus a steady supply of that hand's planets. A single common +Mult joker (a $4 Mad Joker) is not a signal, and one off-plan planet from a pack is not a signal either.
- Use Full House, Straight or Flush only with a real enabler.
- Commit by the end of ante 1-2, and make sure the round player actually plays that hand. Do not let a joker (e.g. Runner) pull plays toward Straights, or spread plays over Full House, Two Pair and High Card. If the jokers you own really support a different hand, commit to that hand by ante 3.
- Take every planet for the main hand (Mercury whenever it is offered). Do not spend money on off-plan planets. Exception: when a pack you already opened (free or paid) has no main-hand planet, take the planet for a related hand (Two Pair, Three of a Kind, Full House) rather than nothing. That insures you against The Eye and The Mouth.
- Targets: level 2-3 by the ante 2 boss (buy at least one main-hand planet before it), 3-5 by antes 3-4, 6-9 by antes 5-6. Once the hand is at target, planets stop counting as progress. Send the surplus toward xMult instead. While the board has no reliable xMult, do not keep building planet infrastructure for a hand already at target: $38 of Telescope and packs took Pair to level 8 while the outlook still showed a cliff.
- While below target: buy the main-hand planet on sight ($3-4). Take one Celestial look per shop before any joker reroll, and always buy the planet before a 2nd reroll in the same shop. Cap rerolls at about $10 per ante unless you hold $60+. Below level 3 at ante 3, or below level 4 at ante 4, planets also come before holding interest above $25. Take a Meteor Tag when it comes free, but do not skip a blind in antes 2-4 just for one, because the shop you give up could show an xMult.
- Reroll budget: if $10 of rerolls in one ante has not found an xMult, put the rest of the surplus into main-hand planets (single planets, Celestial packs) until the hand reaches target. Levels are certain progress; rerolls are a lottery.
- Celestial packs: once the main-hand planet shows up in shops, buy it there for $3 rather than chasing it through packs (6 packs for $26 gave only 2 Mercury). While below target, open a Celestial pack if you keep $20+ after it, or about $10-15 once $25 is covered, and nothing better is on offer. A voucher that fixes the run (Director's Cut) always comes first. Prefer packs to rerolls and to $6+ flat jokers and slow scalers. Buy Normal packs, not Mega, unless 2+ planets in the Mega pack are on-plan. Do not pass packs because 'Mercury is only 25%'. Never open one that leaves you unable to fix the coming blind.
- If the main hand's planets have not shown up after two antes (by ante 3), switch to a drawable hand whose planets you keep being offered. If Pair jokers are on the board, that means Pair: buy the Mercury you were turning down.
- Telescope and Planet Merchant pay off only when about 3+ Celestial packs will follow them, or with Constellation. When that is the plan and the main hand is committed, buy Telescope in antes 2-4 even if it costs one interest tier. Passing it at ante 2 led to 5 packs (about $26) that gave only off-plan planets. Do not buy it for a hand already at target while the board still lacks xMult. Below target with no pack plan, spend that $10 on direct main-hand planets first.

In antes 1-2, survival beats interest until the board has 2 lasting, unconditional scoring jokers (+Mult or chips that fire on ordinary hands) and the main hand is level 2 or higher. Survival means every blind of the current ante, including its boss: treat a boss reading below about 85% as a failing blind, even if the next blind reads 97%. When the current blind already reads 95%+ and the boss is safe too, do not pay for perishable or off-plan jokers, packs or rerolls. Until those 2 scorers are in place:
- Do not leave a shop holding $15+ while a blind of this ante is failing. Spend down to about $10. In ante 1, go below $10 only if a blind of this ante would fail, or if the next ante's Small Blind already reads below about 30%. In that case reroll or buy scorers down to about $5-8.
- Take a joker that scores now over a scaler that starts at 0 (e.g. Red Card), even if the scorer is a rental (see the rentals rule).
- Cheap +Mult stopgaps (Jolly, Raised Fist, Gros Michel, or any joker with a perishable sticker) are a bridge only when the current blind fails without them. Otherwise take a non-perishable scorer even if it is slightly weaker. Never let two stopgaps expire in the same ante or right at a boss.
- Use the Yellow Deck head start on Buffoon packs only as part of a plan to reach $25 by ante 3. In ante 1, open one only if you could still afford a shop joker or a reroll after a miss. If the pack misses, the next shop is a forced search for a scorer, not a place to save.
- Every joker slot and pack pick goes to scoring. Do not take utility or economy jokers (Drunkard, Chaos, Splash, Mail-In Rebate, To the Moon, Cloud 9, Certificate) or a $10 voucher like Grabber.
- Zero scoring jokers before any blind from the ante 1 Big Blind on is an emergency. Buy any affordable scorer. If there is none, do one $5 reroll, then open an Arcana pack (Judgement). Never enter a blind with an empty board while holding $10+.
- With no scoring jokers, play for the biggest base hand you can draw (see the in-blind pace rule) and take pack jokers that pay off now (Runner over Certificate).
- An early xMult (e.g. Card Sharp) must be followed at once by an unconditional base joker and a main-hand planet.
- Take a value generator only when the next boss is safe by the conservative check.
Once the 2 lasting scorers are in place, bank: aim for $25 by the end of ante 2, and hold $25 from ante 3.

Reroll limits:
- At most 2 rerolls per shop, and only 1 in an ante the outlook shows as safe. Spread them across shops. Never chain escalating rerolls ($5, $6, $7, $8) in one shop. Pay for a joker on offer rather than for more looks at the shop.
- Ante 1: do not reroll or spend below about $10 unless a blind of this ante would fail (boss below about 85% counts). The exception is a thin board (fewer than 2 scorers) with the next ante's Small Blind below about 30%: then go down to about $5-8 to find a scorer. With a safe ante, do not reroll below $20. The single emergency reroll on an empty board before a blind is allowed; never chain a second one. Otherwise leave ante 1 with $10-15 so the ante 2 shops can buy two scorers.
- In antes 1-2, never spend $15+ rerolling one shop.
- In a safe ante, do not reroll if it drops you below the next $5 interest tier.
- Once 2 lasting scorers exist, never reroll below $20 unless the NEXT blind reads below 70%, or the severe-forecast exception in the interest rule applies. A mild bad forecast 1-2 antes out (boss around 30-70%) is a reason to keep interest and buy planets, not to empty the bank on rerolls.
- If the main hand is below its level target, take a Celestial look first and cap rerolls at about $10 per ante. If $10 of rerolls in one ante has found no xMult, stop and put the surplus into main-hand planets.
- Buy money-scaling jokers (Bull, Bootstraps) only if you will really hold $25+. Do not buy them on a plan that spends heavily on rerolls or rentals. While you own one, check the next-blind outlook after each spend. Stop if it would fall below about 85% or drop more than 5 points. Spending that breaks the next blind while chasing a later one is not survival.
- From ante 3, reroll only with money above $25 ($28 with a rental, $31 with two), and only if you can open a slot: know which joker you would sell before you reroll. Below $20 at ante 3+, do not reroll at all outside the severe-forecast exception (rerolling $15 to $10 to $5 at ante 4 left $2 at ante 5).
- Stop once one shop has used about $20 on rerolls. Never pay $8-10 for a reroll unless you hold $60+.
Never rerolling at all is also a failure. While the board has fewer than 2 multipliers, use 1-2 $5 rerolls per shop with money above the floor, in the early shops of the ante rather than the boss shop. If the boss itself is the problem, first look for a fix aimed at that boss (Director's Cut, glass from Justice, a skip that avoids it).

Rentals and debt. A rental's real price is $3 times the rounds you will keep it (about 20 rounds from ante 2, so about $15-20+ even for a $1 rental), not its sticker. Compare that with a Celestial pack plus a reroll. A rental also raises the money floor to $28, which blocks rerolls for the rest of the run.
Ante 1: buy no rentals, even at $1, unless the current blind fails without one. The other exceptions:
- The board has no scoring joker and either the ante's boss reads below about 90% or ante 2's Small Blind reads below about 50%. Then a rental that scores now (e.g. Half Joker on Pair) beats a scaler that starts at 0. Yellow Deck can carry one rental.
- You hold an xMult with no base. Then a big flat-chips rental (Stuntman +250) or an affordable Bootstraps is worth it.
Antes 2-4: carry at most one rental. Buy one only if the next blind reads below 70% without it, or under the xMult exception. A flat +Mult rental (Green Joker, Seltzer, Raised Fist) bought while the ante reads 90%+ is never worth it. Never take a rental for flat Mult when a non-rental fix exists, such as Director's Cut for a bad boss. Never take a money-scaling rental (Bull) in antes 1-4 unless you will really keep $28+, even when it is free from a pack. Rent plus spending down makes it weaker every round (Bull ended at +10 chips on $5). From ante 3, one lasting rental that is a core scorer for the main hand (Hanging Chad, Even Steven on an even-heavy deck) is acceptable only with a free slot and $28 banked. Never take a new rental below $20. If a second rental is the only survival fix, sell one at the first shop where the next blind reads 85%+ without it. Never carry two across an ante below $31.
xMult exception: from ante 2, if the board has no xMult and an upcoming boss reads below 50%, an affordable rental xMult that fires on every main-hand play (Cavendish, Card Sharp on a repeated hand, Baseball with Uncommons, Acrobat, Vampire) beats any flat +Mult option. Accept an eternal rental only for such an every-hand xMult when nothing sellable is available. Never use the exception for a periodic or conditional xMult (Loyalty Card fires about once in 6 hands; The Order on an uncommitted hand). Refuse it too if you already carry a rental.
Always:
- With a rental, the floor is $28, not $25. Never spend to $0 while holding one: the fee puts you into debt and locks you out of the next shops.
- Never use Credit Card or debt to pay for scoring in antes 1-3. At $0 or below, buy no rentals.
- Never take a rental that is perishable or decaying (Popcorn, Ice Cream, Ramen). Never carry a third rental.
- Sell a survival rental as soon as the blind you rented it for is behind you, unless the outlook shows you still need it. Sell it before any other joker once a non-rental scorer can replace it, or once the next blind is 90%+ safe without it. Do not keep a shrinking rental (an Ice Cream rental kept from 100 down to 15 chips).
- Do not let the $28/$31 floor block buys that improve the build.
- Before a boss that costs money (The Tooth, $1 per card), enter with cash for the cards you expect to play + $3 per rental + $5. Play 4-card hands or as few hands as possible.

Judge a board by its reliable scoring. The outlook is simulated with the boss's effect and the build as it is, but it still averages over lucky draws, and it can glitch.
- When reaching the target depends on a conditional joker (suit, rank or hand-type jokers, Flower Pot, Idol, Ancient, Castle) or on unreliable pieces, treat the boss as less safe than shown. If the whole board is one conditional joker (e.g. Wrathful, which fires on 13 of 52 cards), read 95% as about 85% for skip, reroll and leave-shop decisions. Lower it further when the boss debuffs cards or cuts hand options (The Head, The Goad).
- Do not trust a high outlook on an empty board. With zero jokers and every hand at level 1, even a 300-chip Small Blind rated 98% has been lost. Play it by the in-blind pace rule, not as already won. Treat any blind of 450 or more as below 80%, whatever the simulator says. If a jokerless blind falls behind (a weak first hand), drop all shop planning and play only for the chip target.
- Check a reading that jumps or drops with no change to the board or the blind before acting on it, especially one you already flagged as an artifact. Query it again, or compare it with the round player's clear estimate. Never let an unchecked low reading trigger 'survival overrides interest' and a full spend: a suspect 12% on The Wheel drove $17 to $0, and the round player then put The Wheel at about 100%.
- Before each ante step (especially 3 to 4, which is x2.8), check that the next ante's Small Blind is not already below 70% in the outlook. If it is, keep buying lasting scoring even if it costs an interest tier.

Unreliable scoring is backup, not the plan. That includes perishable jokers, decaying ones (Ice Cream, Popcorn, Seltzer, Turtle Bean), random ones (Misprint), time-limited ones (Seltzer, 10 hands; Ramen) and destroyable ones (Gros Michel, 1 in 6).
- A perishable fixes only the blinds it will still be alive for. Count its remaining rounds against the first blind the outlook marks as failing. If it expires before that blind, the problem is not solved: keep searching for a permanent xMult at the same priority and keep money ready for it. A perishable Duo or Blueprint does not cover the multiplier gap. Start looking for a permanent replacement 2 rounds before expiry. If it is your only xMult (Ramen x2), plan its replacement from the moment you take it.
- Never let two perishables expire in the same ante or right at a boss.
- If the current ante reads 80%+ and the danger is the next ante (the outlook flags a cliff 1-2 antes out), buy no stopgaps at all: no perishables, no small conditional +Mult, no rentals, and no skips for packs that only offer perishables. Spend only on lasting pieces (xMult, main-hand planets, deck shaping), and hold $25 from ante 3. Stopgaps bought and sold one shop later drained $50 to $18 and left nothing for the second xMult. A rental Wily and a perishable Golden Joker as patches against a 0-5% forecast had the same result.
- Replace a shrinking chips joker before it falls to about half its value (Ice Cream below about 75 chips).
- From ante 3, treat a flat joker that scores under 10% of the hand as a slot to free. Sell it as soon as the shop offers anything better for the main hand.
- If more than half the board's scoring is unreliable, work out the bad case: Gros Michel gone, Misprint at about +5, decay after 4 more hands. Keep buying lasting scoring until the boss clears without those pieces.
- Never let a perishable or rental joker be your only chips source.

Interest against forecasts (once 2 lasting scorers exist; before that, the survival rule applies). When every blind in the current ante reads 90%+ and the forecast is only mildly bad (a boss 1-2 antes away around 30-70%, with a reasonable board), do not reroll or buy speculative packs below $25 ($28 with a rental). 'Survival first' then covers only the current ante's blinds, or the next blind when it reads below 70%. A high outlook that rests on a variable joker (Ancient, Idol, Castle), or a boss that hides information, is no reason to spend the bank either. From ante 4, while the current ante reads 95%+, spend only the surplus above $25 ($28 with a rental) and never drop below $20, so ante 5 can still buy a fix. A reroll plus a Mega Celestial at 99%/95% took $29 to $17, and ante 5 then opened at $20 against a 0% boss and stayed broke for three antes.
Severe-forecast exception, which applies especially with no xMult:
- Next ante's boss below about 50%: spend down to the $25 tier in every shop of the current ante.
- Next ante's boss below about 30%, or any blind of the next ante below about 20%: the interest floor no longer applies. Spend down to about $15 plus $3 per rental, and no lower, so the cliff ante still has rerolls. Runs that entered the cliff ante at $9-13 could not reroll in the ante that killed them.
- If the outlook has shown the next ante at 0-10% for two antes in a row, the build lacks a multiplier. Planets and perishables will not fix it. Start $5 xMult rerolls now.
Act in the current ante's shops that still have a blind after them, while rerolls still cost $5. Do not save the money for the dying ante: arriving there and spending $28 down to $7 with only 1-2 shops left found nothing. Spend only on things that directly add xMult or main-hand levels:
- one or two $5 xMult rerolls per shop
- Buffoon packs
- main-hand planets, and Celestial packs while below the level target (or with Telescope)
Spectral and random Arcana packs and one-card tarots do not count as fixing a forecast. The exception is an Arcana aimed at a named edit on trigger cards (glass or steel). $30 down to $9 on a Spectral and an Arcana Jumbo added no multiplier. Do not dump the money into escalating rerolls in one shop.
When the boss is below 50% and you dip into survival money, judge each $ by how much it raises the boss estimate. Prefer a main-hand planet already in the shop, then joker rerolls. If two buys in a row miss, stop and keep the interest.

From ante 2 to ante 5, while the board has fewer than 2 multiplier sources, spend all surplus above $25 in every shop. A suit-dependent x1.5 such as Ancient counts as half. Loyalty Card and other periodic xMult do not count: with 4 hands it fires about once every 1.5 rounds, and it may never fire against a boss like The Eye. Spending means 1-2 $5 rerolls spread across shops, Buffoon packs, and xMult or +Mult jokers. If the main hand is below its level target, buy its planet first. Once the hand is at target, more planets, planet infrastructure (Telescope, extra Celestial packs) and hand-boosting +Mult (Supernova) are not progress, so all surplus goes to rerolls and Buffoon packs for xMult until one reliable every-hand xMult is on the board. A run that rerolled only twice and put $38 into Pair levels kept seeing a cliff one ante ahead.
- Never pass a real xMult (The Idol, Cavendish, Card Sharp, Acrobat and similar) just to keep an interest tier while a slot is open, or because of a rental or eternal sticker (see the rentals rule). Empty slots never grow.
- With empty slots and money above $25 in antes 2-3, buy durable, non-rental scorers that fit the main hand (Raised Fist, Sly, Castle or Greedy when the deck feeds them). Do not pass them while waiting for an xMult. A full board buys time to find the multiplier and prevents panic rental buys at ante 4.
- Do not swap one flat +Mult or chips joker for another as a fix. It only counts if the outlook rises.
- Joker Stencil is a stopgap: take any xMult, scaling or growing joker even if it lowers Stencil, and judge it by the score needed 1-2 antes ahead.
- Do not spend this surplus on Arcana, Spectral or Standard packs that add one-card tweaks, or on Golden Joker or other economy, unless you are aiming at a specific card the build needs.
- Spend a windfall of $20+ over target (Investment Tag, big interest) this way before the Small Blind, spread across that ante's shops.

Buy only jokers that fire on what you actually play and own. Before turning a joker down, check its condition against the main hand.
- No jokers for a different hand type (Droll/Crafty for Flush, Crazy or Devious for Straight, Zany for Three of a Kind, Clever for Two Pair) as a bridge or as filler. Buy unconditional +Mult or chips instead (Abstract, Banner, Popcorn; Jolly and Half Joker when Pair is the main hand, since a 2-card Pair always meets '3 or fewer cards'), or reroll to find one. Not Blackboard, a conditional xMult that needs held Spades/Clubs.
- This applies to conditional xMult too. Do not buy The Order, The Tribe, The Family and similar for a hand you are not committed to, or cannot draw reliably (a Straight with no Shortcut or Four Fingers). This matters even more when the buy drops you below $10. An $8 Order on a Pair board was dead weight, and selling it raised the boss read.
- Jokers tied to face cards or ranks (Photograph, Scary Face) fire only on some Pairs, so they are weaker than they look. No jokers that need cards you lack (Stone Joker with no Stone cards). Early on, skip conditional support (Mime without a strong held-in-hand card).
- Early on, buy jokers that scale, multiply or add plain +Mult. Prefer one that scores now over a scaler starting at 0. If the shop has none, keep the money rather than filling slots with conditional or off-hand jokers.
- Buy for the smaller side. Before buying a scorer, compare the board's typical chips and Mult on the main hand. Once Mult is above about 30 and chips are under about 100, another +Mult is nearly worthless. Buy chips (main-hand planets, Stuntman, Hiker, Blue Joker, Square, Ice Cream, Bull) or xMult instead, and skip flat +Mult even when it is free. From ante 5, a board with 2+ +Mult jokers and an xMult but no chips joker, scoring under about 200 chips on the main hand, ranks a lasting chips source (Castle, Stuntman, Bull, Hiker, Blue Joker, Arrowhead, Odd Todd or Scholar for Pair) above another +Mult or planet. Look for it with the ante 5-6 surplus, not in ante 7.
- If you keep a scaler with a trigger you control, feed it on purpose: for Red Card, skip cheap packs whose contents are worth less than +3 Mult, but from ante 3 only with money that stays at $25+. Below $25, open a pack only if it could hold the main-hand planet or an xMult joker. Every $5 below $25 costs $1 a round, and feeding Red Card took $34 to $11 and kept antes 3-4 at $7-15. If you won't feed it, don't keep it while you lack scoring.
- No sideways swaps. Do not sell a flat or conditional joker to buy another of the same kind. From ante 3, do not buy flat or perishable fillers (Swashbuckler) that only nudge a failing boss estimate, unless that joker alone lifts the next blind above about 80%. A swap must add a multiplier, a lasting chips source your deck triggers, or a scaler you will feed for several antes.
- Do not hold scalers that pull against each other on discards. Banner, Green Joker and Mystic Summit want zero discards; Castle and Ramen-style discard users want many. Pick one direction when you buy the second one, and sell or skip the one that conflicts.
- Do not play Straights or Flushes as filler once you have jokers for the main hand and no enabler. In a desperate last shop, do not switch to a hand you can't reliably draw: with 8 cards, 2 discards and no Four Fingers or Shortcut, a Straight in one hand is only about a 25-30% event. The empty-board case is the exception: see the in-blind pace rule.

Crisis cash discipline: when a blind or boss looks lost, every purchase must raise it clearly. That means about +15 points on the boss, or lifting a failing blind above about 50%. A buy that moves a doomed boss from 15% to 20% is not a fix; keep the money for the next shop and the next ante.
- When a boss you must beat is below 50%, spend at most about half your money on rerolls in one shop. Stop when the next reroll would leave under about $12 for the remaining shops before the boss. Each later shop is a fresh roll for xMult, and you need money there to buy the xMult plus a planet.
- While shops remain in the ante, never spend to $0. Keep at least the price of a common xMult ($6) plus $3 per rental due at round end.
- Grabber, Observatory and other vouchers that do not reroll the boss, economy jokers (a perishable Business Card), random Arcana or Celestial packs, off-plan levels and sideways flat-joker swaps do not count as fixes. Director's Cut does count (see the boss rule). Once the next boss reads 10% or less, every dollar goes to rerolls, packs or planets aimed at a multiplier. Count a perishable or rental that expires this ante as already gone. Never spend your last money on a voucher and then skip a blind.
- When the final boss reads 15% or less, stop buying +5% steps, such as $3 off-plan planets just for Constellation's x0.1. Stop buy-then-sell trials too (Splash sold one decision later). Keep $10+ for the last two shops and spend it only on what can multiply the score: a reroll or Buffoon pack aimed at an xMult or big-chips joker, or a Mercury. Four Constellation planets and four empty rerolls took $26 to $0, and the final shops could not afford a single look.
- Flag the run as in trouble as soon as the outlook shows the next ante at 0-15%. React with targeted certain upgrades in the current ante (see the severe-forecast exception), not by emptying the bank in a panic.

Skipping blinds. A skip gives up the blind payout, the unused-hand money, an interest round and a whole shop. Rare, Uncommon, Holographic, Foil, Voucher, Coupon, Polychrome and money tags (Economy, Handy, Investment) pay out only after a later blind, so skipping sends you into the next blind with the same board.
- Do not skip in an ante where the boss is below about 40-50%, or where the boss estimate is likely optimistic (it rests on one conditional joker, an xMult that depends on drawing specific ranks, or a boss that debuffs cards or drains levels like The Head, The Goad or The Arm). Play the last blind before the boss if it is at least 60%, and use that shop to fix the board. Never skip both blinds of an ante into a boss below 50%: a tag that pays after the boss does nothing for it. When you are broke (under about $10), play the blind for its shop and the unused-hand money.
- In antes 1-2, skip for an economy tag (Investment included, despite its reputation as the good ante 1 skip) only on a solid board: at least 2 lasting scorers, or 1 unconditional scorer plus a main-hand planet, and a boss reading 98%+. A 95% read carried by a lone suit joker (Wrathful) does not qualify. In antes 2-4, do not skip for a Meteor or other planet tag; the shop could show an xMult.
- Later, skip the pre-boss blind for a money tag only if the boss has read at least 90% for two or more shops in a row and the shop you give up has nothing you want.
- Never skip for a D6 or other reroll tag while the board lacks scoring, or while the next ante's boss reads low. The rerolls it gives are still a lottery.
- Never skip for a joker tag (Rare, Uncommon, Buffoon, Holographic, Foil) with all slots full unless you have already named a weak non-eternal joker to sell where it pays out. A Rare Tag taken with 5 full slots (one an eternal Riff-Raff) gave nothing and cost a payout and a shop at $9. In that shop, always look at the free joker and sell the weakest or expiring joker (spent Seltzer, decaying Ice Cream, economy, flat filler) to take it if it scores better. When the run is struggling, skip only if the tag itself fixes the next blind.
- When a free pack opens (Meteor, Mega Celestial), always take something: main-hand or Pair planets first, otherwise a related hand's planet.

Eternal jokers are a permanent slot cost. Before any Eternal buy, ask: 'when the xMult shows up, which slot does it go in?'
- Before ante 5, lock at most one slot with a non-xMult Eternal, and only for a scaler that fits the main hand and does not fight the rest of the board. Mystic Summit wants zero discards and works against discard users. Riff-Raff needs empty slots. Never hold more than 2 non-xMult Eternals at any point.
- Never take an Eternal flat or conditional +Mult or chips joker, or an Eternal utility joker, if it would make 2+ Eternal slots. That holds even when it is free from a pack (Swashbuckler, Fibonacci, Supernova, Walkie Talkie). The only exception is a next blind below 50% without it, with nothing else that fixes it. Skip the pick instead: a locked slot is worth more than +4 Mult once you need room for xMult. Eternal is fine on a real xMult.
- From ante 3, and certainly by ante 5, keep at least 2 non-eternal slots you can sell or swap, so the convert-to-xMult step stays possible. Boards with 3-5 Eternal flat scorers could not add an xMult, because every swap lowered the outlook (selling the one free Green Joker dropped a 97% blind to 12%).
- If a blind forces a third Eternal, take the one with the highest ceiling (an xMult, Hanging Chad, a retrigger), not flat Mult. Never take an Eternal rental for flat Mult when a non-rental fix such as Director's Cut exists.
- In antes 1-2, do not lock a slot with an Eternal joker that is flat filler or will be a weak flat effect by ante 4 (Eternal plain Joker, Splash, Sly, Arrowhead, Fibonacci, Blue Joker). Take one only if the next blind is below 70% without it.
- When opening a Buffoon pack with no jokers, rank the choices by how many chips they add to an ordinary hand right now, and take a scorer if there is one. If the pack has no scorer and 4+ slots are free, an economy joker (even an Eternal one like Reserved Parking) still beats wasting the $4, but count it toward the Eternal cap.
- Do not buy a Buffoon pack, or skip for a Buffoon Tag, when every slot is full and the only sellable joker is a key scorer. Decide before paying what you would sell; otherwise spend on a planet or keep the interest.

Selling jokers, and outlook noise.
- Keep your xMult. Never sell a permanent xMult joker (Card Sharp, The Idol, Seeing Double, a permanent x3 Flower Pot, etc.) for a perishable or decaying joker (Turtle Bean, Popcorn, Ice Cream, Seltzer, Ramen), even if the sim says it fixes the current boss. Selling Seeing Double for Turtle Bean lifted one boss from 41% to 86%, but the Bean was worth $3 by ante 7 and ante 8 was played with a single xMult. Do not sell an xMult for a flat or scaling +Mult joker unless the boss you are about to face is impossible with it, and never for a joker that adds no score (Juggler, Splash, economy). If one boss needs a fix, sell a flat, expiring or rental joker, or spend money. From ante 6, the count of permanent xMult jokers should only go up (target 2+ by ante 7). Be suspicious of a short-term outlook jump from a hand-size joker when the next ante needs a multiplier. Before any swap that removes a multiplier, compare the next ante's outlook with and without the swap, not just the next blind's. $3 a round in rent for an x3 is cheap, and one reliable xMult is worth about +2.5 blinds.
- Do not sell a working, still-growing +Mult joker for a trigger xMult (Loyalty Card and other every-N-hands jokers) unless it fires on most boss attempts. Divide N by the hands you actually play per round: if it fires less than about once every two rounds, it is not a multiplier for planning. Red Card at +9 sold for Loyalty left ante 5 reading 10%/0%, and Loyalty was sold six decisions later.
- In the last shop before a blind, never sell a scoring joker if that blind's read goes down, unless it still reads 95%+ afterward. Abstract Joker loses +3 Mult for every joker sold. A boss estimate means nothing if you die on the blind before it: selling Banner to lift the boss from 52% to 59% dropped a 100% Small Blind to 51%, and the run lost that blind.
- Treat outlook changes under about 10 points as noise (boss reads swing 40-65% from shop to shop on an unchanged board). Never trade a known, lasting effect (a joker, a slot, a blind's payout) for a small simulated gain.
- Conditional xMult like Flower Pot is still a bonus, not the engine. It checks only scoring cards, so a kicker never helps. Two Pair covers all four suits only about 1 time in 6, and Full House about half the time. Do not pick the main hand around it, and do not accept an outlook that depends on it firing. When it struggles against one boss, change how you play (five-card hands that cover all four suits, Wild cards) rather than selling it.
- If your only xMult needs a hand that is hard to draw with 2 discards (The Trio, The Family, Four of a Kind), shape the deck at once with Strength, Death or Hanged Man to pile cards onto a few ranks. Keep the scorer for the hand you actually draw most (do not sell the Mad Joker powering Two Pair) until the deck can make the target hand. Otherwise stay on Pair.

Score the build against the actual boss, and keep a way to change bosses.
- Once the boss is shown, rate every shop of the ante against its rule, not against the Small or Big Blind. For a one-hand boss like The Needle, only per-hand +Mult, xMult and main-hand planets count. Skip delayed or counter jokers (Loyalty Card, Ride the Bus, Runner, Wee, Lucky Cat) and economy until the one-hand score clears. A boss debuff (e.g. The Goad on Spades) applies only to the boss, so play normally in the Small and Big Blinds.
- Against The Arm, never play the levelled main hand. Before the round, name one off-plan sacrifice hand (High Card or a spare hand), lock the round player to it (override Card Sharp/Burglar 'repeat the hand' logic), and clear in as few hands as you can. Hold main-hand planets and any Fool until after The Arm. Playing Pair into The Arm took it from level 6 to level 2.
- Director's Cut: from ante 4, if it is in the shop and you have $10 above your interest floor, buy it before any reroll or pack. This matters most when the current boss or the next ante's boss reads below 50%, or when the engine has a boss it cannot beat (Card Sharp or Burglar repeat plans against The Eye, The Arm, The Psychic). Get it by ante 5-6 at the latest. A boss reroll is a lasting fix; $10 of rerolls is a gamble. Leaving it in the shop for 6 decisions with $31-50 in hand led to death against a 29-40% Pillar.
- Buy other vouchers only if they work with the engine you already have. Observatory is dead money with Constellation, because planets are used at once instead of held. Hieroglyph and Petroglyph are not worth draining the bank to $15.
- In any round rated below about 95%, turn off grow_joker style goals and play the highest score each hand. Grow scalers only on blinds that are about 100% safe. Do not buy fresh slow scalers (Square, Wee, Runner) at ante 3+ unless they can be fed for free.

In-blind pace rule: play each blind to its chip target.
- Before every hand, work out chips still needed ÷ hands left (a 300 blind over 4 hands needs 75 per hand). If the best hand you can play now won't keep that pace, discard toward a bigger hand while discards remain, even if that breaks a pair you already hold.
- With only 2 discards at Gold, use them early, while 3-4 hands remain to play what they dig up.
- On a blank board (no jokers, every hand at level 1), Pair is not the plan. A level-1 Pair scores about 30-64 and Two Pair about 60-80, both below pace. Dig for Three of a Kind (about 100-180), a Straight (about 200-260) or a Flush (about 250-300). Play a lone Pair or High Card only when it keeps pace or finishes the blind as the last hand.
- If the score after hand 2 is below 50% of the target, switch to the highest-variance line available (discard toward a Flush or Straight).
- Treat losing a blind rated 90%+ as a play error and audit it. Log every hand and discard as its own decision: cards, expected score, running total, chips still needed, hands and discards left.
